$comment: THE ONE RULE for a well-formed X-Correlation-Id, on all three deployables and on the queues.
A correlation identifier is untrusted: it correlates and authorizes nothing. What it must not do
is carry markup, whitespace or control characters into a header, a problem body or a log line.
Each stack implements the rule itself - no shared library crosses a deployable boundary - and
each stack's suite asserts its implementation against the vectors below:
The rules used to differ - RagCore accepted any printable string, .NET letters/digits/._-, the
Integrations Service hex only - so one journey's identifier was kept on one hop and replaced on
the next, and an integration command could be dead-lettered for an identifier RagCore accepted.
